footer.topicText: This quiz takes you through quick anatomy trivia rounds about the parts of the body most people know: bones and joints, muscles, blood, breathing, digestion, senses, organs, and body systems.
footer.aboutText: The questions are built to feel like fast pub-quiz trivia, with simple body facts, a few trickier final clues, and short explanations after each answer. It is made for general knowledge, entertainment, and self-challenge only. It is not medical advice, diagnosis, professional training, or a clinical assessment. If you have health concerns, speak to a qualified healthcare professional.

stageGroups.title: Body Basics
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice start. Now let's see how well you know the body frame underneath it all.

questions.prompt: Which organ never really gets a day off pumping blood?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through vessels so oxygen and nutrients can travel around the body.

questions.prompt: What is actually the largest organ in your body?
questions.explanation: Skin is the body's largest organ and forms a protective outer layer.

questions.prompt: About how many bones does an adult human usually have?
questions.explanation: Most adults have 206 bones, though tiny natural variations can happen.

questions.prompt: Which part of the body hides the smallest bones?
questions.explanation: The three tiny bones in the middle ear are the smallest bones in the body.

questions.prompt: What is your rib cage mainly guarding?
questions.explanation: The rib cage helps protect the heart and lungs inside the chest.

questions.prompt: Which organ is mostly responsible for filtering blood?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood and help remove waste through urine.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells are basically your body's oxygen couriers?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, which helps carry oxygen.

questions.prompt: What is the bend in the middle of your arm called?
questions.explanation: The elbow is the joint where the upper arm and forearm meet.

stageGroups.title: Bones And Joints
stageGroups.encouragement: Strong frame. Next up: the muscles that actually make the body move.

questions.prompt: Which bony shield protects your brain?
questions.explanation: The skull is the bony case that protects the brain.

questions.prompt: Which bone wins the title of longest in the body?
questions.explanation: The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest bone in the body.

questions.prompt: What is the common name for the patella?
questions.explanation: The patella is the kneecap at the front of the knee joint.

questions.prompt: Where would you find the metacarpal bones?
questions.explanation: Metacarpals are the bones in the palm area of the hand.

questions.prompt: What connects a muscle to a bone?
questions.explanation: Tendons attach muscles to bones so movement can happen.

questions.prompt: What smooth tissue keeps many joints from grinding bone on bone?
questions.explanation: Cartilage helps reduce friction and cushion joints where bones meet.

questions.prompt: What do we call the place where two bones meet?
questions.explanation: A joint is the place where two or more bones meet.

questions.prompt: The spine is made of a stack of bones called what?
questions.explanation: Vertebrae are the bones that form the spine.

stageGroups.title: Muscles And Movement
stageGroups.encouragement: You are moving well. Now the quiz checks your heart, blood, and pulse knowledge.

questions.prompt: Which muscle quietly helps every breath happen?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm moves down and up to help air move in and out of the lungs.

questions.prompt: Which muscle is on the front of the upper arm?
questions.explanation: The biceps sit on the front of the upper arm and help bend the elbow.

questions.prompt: Where are your hamstrings?
questions.explanation: The hamstrings are a group of muscles at the back of the thigh.

questions.prompt: What do muscles usually do to create movement?
questions.explanation: Muscles create movement by contracting, or shortening.

questions.prompt: Which muscles do the work when you rise onto tiptoe?
questions.explanation: The calf muscles help lift the heel when you stand on tiptoe.

questions.prompt: Which shoulder muscle gives the upper arm its rounded shape?
questions.explanation: The deltoid is the rounded muscle over the shoulder.

questions.prompt: Which body part contains muscles that help you smile?
questions.explanation: Facial muscles create expressions such as smiling and frowning.

questions.prompt: Which muscles are on the front of the thigh?
questions.explanation: The quadriceps are the major muscle group on the front of the thigh.

stageGroups.title: Heart And Blood
stageGroups.encouragement: Good pulse. Take a breath — the next round is all lungs and airways.

questions.prompt: How many chambers are working inside the human heart?
questions.explanation: The human heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to the body or lungs.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessels usually carry blood back to the heart?
questions.explanation: Veins usually carry blood back toward the heart.

questions.prompt: What are the tiny blood vessels where the real exchange happens?
questions.explanation: Capillaries are tiny vessels where exchange with tissues can happen.

questions.prompt: When you check your pulse, what rhythm are you feeling?
questions.explanation: A pulse is the rhythm you can feel as the heartbeat pushes blood through arteries.

questions.prompt: Which blood parts help with clotting?
questions.explanation: Platelets help blood form clots after small injuries.

questions.prompt: What is the liquid part of blood called?
questions.explanation: Plasma is the liquid part of blood that carries cells and other substances.

questions.prompt: Which side of the heart sends blood to the lungs?
questions.explanation: The right side of the heart pumps blood toward the lungs.

stageGroups.title: Lungs And Breathing
stageGroups.encouragement: Fresh air. Now let's see how fast your brain and nerves can keep up.

questions.prompt: Which organs do the heavy lifting when you take in oxygen?
questions.explanation: The lungs bring oxygen into the body and help remove carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: What is the windpipe also called?
questions.explanation: The trachea is the windpipe that carries air toward the lungs.

questions.prompt: What are the tiny air sacs where oxygen meets the blood?
questions.explanation: Alveoli are tiny air sacs where oxygen and carbon dioxide can move between air and blood.

questions.prompt: Which gas do you mainly breathe in for your cells to use?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the gas your cells need for releasing energy from food.

questions.prompt: Which gas do you breathe out as a waste product?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a waste gas that leaves the body when you breathe out.

questions.prompt: When the diaphragm moves down, what usually happens?
questions.explanation: When the diaphragm moves down, the chest has more space and air can move in.

questions.prompt: What does the nose help do before air reaches the lungs?
questions.explanation: The nose helps warm, moisten, and filter air as you breathe in.

questions.prompt: Which tubes branch from the trachea into the lungs?
questions.explanation: The bronchi are the main airways that branch into the lungs.

stageGroups.title: Brain And Nerves
stageGroups.encouragement: Quick thinking. Now follow the food route and catch the digestion clues.

questions.prompt: Which organ is the body's command center?
questions.explanation: The brain controls and coordinates many body activities.

questions.prompt: What carries messages between the brain and body?
questions.explanation: Nerves carry signals between the brain, spinal cord, and the rest of the body.

questions.prompt: Which structure runs down the back inside the spine?
questions.explanation: The spinal cord carries nerve signals between the brain and body.

questions.prompt: Which reaction is your nervous system acting in a flash?
questions.explanation: A reflex is a fast automatic response to a signal.

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain is strongly linked with balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum helps coordinate movement and balance.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a basic nerve cell?
questions.explanation: A neuron is a nerve cell that can send and receive signals.

questions.prompt: Which sense is linked most directly to the optic nerve?
questions.explanation: The optic nerve carries visual information from the eye to the brain.

questions.prompt: Which body system includes the brain, spinal cord, and nerves?
questions.explanation: The nervous system includes the brain, spinal cord, and nerves.

stageGroups.title: Digestion And Nutrients
stageGroups.encouragement: You handled the food route. Next up: eyes, ears, skin, and a few sneaky sense clues.

questions.prompt: Which organ produces enzymes that help digest food?
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces digestive enzymes as well as hormones such as insulin.

questions.prompt: Where are most nutrients absorbed from digested food?
questions.explanation: Most nutrient absorption happens in the small intestine.

questions.prompt: Which organ makes bile to help break down fats?
questions.explanation: The liver makes bile, which helps the body digest fats.

questions.prompt: Which small organ stores bile?
questions.explanation: The gallbladder stores bile made by the liver.

questions.prompt: What tube carries food from the mouth to the stomach?
questions.explanation: The esophagus moves swallowed food down to the stomach.

questions.prompt: Which organ helps control blood sugar by making insulin?
questions.explanation: The pancreas makes insulin, a hormone involved in blood sugar control.

questions.prompt: Which part of the digestive tract absorbs most water from leftover food?
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and helps form solid waste.

questions.prompt: Which tiny finger-like structures help the small intestine absorb nutrients?
questions.explanation: Villi increase the surface area of the small intestine so nutrients can be absorbed.

stageGroups.title: Senses And Skin
stageGroups.encouragement: Sharp senses. Now the questions start mixing organs, systems, and body jobs.

questions.prompt: Which part of the eye controls how much light enters?
questions.explanation: The pupil changes size to let more or less light into the eye.

questions.prompt: Which part of the eye focuses light onto the retina?
questions.explanation: The lens helps focus incoming light onto the retina.

questions.prompt: Which part of the body has tiny bones that help with hearing?
questions.explanation: The middle ear contains three tiny bones that help pass along sound vibrations.

questions.prompt: Which old idea about taste is a common myth?
questions.explanation: The old tongue taste map is oversimplified; taste receptors are not divided into neat zones.

questions.prompt: Which skin structures help cool the body?
questions.explanation: Sweat glands release sweat, which can help cool the body as it evaporates.

questions.prompt: Which pigment helps give skin, hair, and eyes much of their color?
questions.explanation: Melanin is a pigment that contributes to skin, hair, and eye color.

questions.prompt: Which sense uses receptors in the nose?
questions.explanation: Smell uses receptors in the nose that detect chemicals in the air.

questions.prompt: Which body part contains the retina?
questions.explanation: The retina is a light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.

stageGroups.title: Organs And Systems
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice all-body thinking. Final round now — this is where the easy points disappear.

questions.prompt: Which valve-like flap helps stop food going down the windpipe?
questions.explanation: The epiglottis helps cover the airway when you swallow.

questions.prompt: Which organ is known for making many important blood proteins?
questions.explanation: The liver makes many proteins that the blood and body use.

questions.prompt: Which system helps recognize and fight germs?
questions.explanation: The immune system helps recognize and fight germs and other unwanted invaders.

questions.prompt: Which small structures can swell when the immune system is active?
questions.explanation: Lymph nodes are part of the immune system and can become larger during immune activity.

questions.prompt: Which hormone-making system sends chemical messages around the body?
questions.explanation: The endocrine system includes glands that release hormones.

questions.prompt: Which organ stores glycogen and helps process nutrients?
questions.explanation: The liver stores glycogen and helps process nutrients after digestion.

questions.prompt: Which body system moves oxygen and nutrients through the blood?
questions.explanation: The circulatory system moves blood around the body.

questions.prompt: Which system includes skin, hair, and nails?
questions.explanation: The integumentary system includes the skin, hair, nails, and related structures.

questions.prompt: Which term means closer to the head?
questions.explanation: Superior means higher or closer to the head in anatomy.

questions.prompt: Which term means toward the front of the body?
questions.explanation: Anterior means toward the front of the body.

questions.prompt: Which term means farther from the center of the body?
questions.explanation: Distal means farther from the point of attachment or the body's center.

questions.prompt: What is the common name for the clavicle?
questions.explanation: The clavicle is commonly called the collarbone.

questions.prompt: When you bump the inside of your elbow, which nerve causes that sharp tingle?
questions.explanation: That zap-like feeling usually comes from the ulnar nerve as it passes near the upper-arm bone at the elbow.

questions.prompt: Which organ has tiny filtering units called nephrons?
questions.explanation: Nephrons are tiny filtering units inside the kidneys.

questions.prompt: Which structure carries urine from a kidney to the bladder?
questions.explanation: A ureter carries urine from a kidney down to the bladder.

questions.prompt: Which plane divides the body into left and right sections?
questions.explanation: A sagittal plane divides the body into left and right sections.
